findings.public_requirement: Two transistor-level input TIA branches with DC-overload cancellation must accept inp and inn and preserve the specified input bias and overload behavior.
findings.electrical_reason: Each input drives a common-base NPN and cascode/load path, followed by an emitter follower into the RF chain. Each input also has a MOS current sink whose gate is driven by a low-frequency output-referred feedback path: finalp/finaln are divided onto fp/fn, compared in the cross-coupled OTA/mirror stages, and converted by Xcs_p/Xcs_n into gdc_p/gdc_n. Thus the cancellation controls are electrically connected to the input current-sink terminals rather than decorative. The nominal and overload measurements show matched input bias and a finite, well-controlled overload operating point.

findings.public_requirement: Two transistor-level gain-controlled RF stages must provide monotonic gain control and the specified transimpedance, bandwidth, and group delay.
findings.electrical_reason: The first and second stages are separate differential NPN common-emitter stages with emitter-degeneration/tail nodes et1 and et2, resonant collector loads, emitter-follower interstage interfaces, and distinct NMOS tail devices. In both stages Xmg_v1/Xmg_v2 place a gc-controlled current path in parallel with the oa-biased tail path, so gc changes transistor current and stage transconductance rather than merely feeding an unused node. The AC sweep's nonzero gain span and monotonic gain response corroborate the connected control mechanism; gain and delay target misses are sizing/bias performance issues, not absence of either RF stage.

findings.public_requirement: A transistor-level differential output buffer must drive outp and outn from bufinp and bufinn with the specified amplitude and distortion behavior.
findings.electrical_reason: Xq_bp and Xq_bn form an actively biased differential BJT output stage: bufinp/bufinn drive their bases, their emitters reach the common NMOS-tail node through R_dbp/R_dbn, and their collectors drive outp/outn against 50-ohm supply loads. R_xf and R_xn carry those active output nodes to finalp/finaln with negligible series resistance; they are not an input-to-output passive feedthrough. The direct buffer tests produce substantial differential output at both applied input amplitudes, confirming the active signal path even though the measured amplitude and THD are not at all numerical targets.

findings.public_requirement: A transistor-level peak detector must accept pkdinp and pkdinn and produce a strictly increasing differential detector response at detp and detn.
findings.electrical_reason: The two RF inputs are biased about pkdcm and drive paired NPN emitter-follower rectifier devices sharing pke. R_pke/C_pke provide the stored/decaying detected quantity, while Xq_rpp/Xq_rpn and R_pker/C_pker provide an active replica reference. Xq_da_p/Xq_da_n then compare pke against pker in an actively tailed differential stage and develop filtered outputs detp/detn through collector loads. The 50-mV direct test produces a nonzero 44.7-mV differential detector result, demonstrating a real detector-to-output path. The adverse high-amplitude and monotonicity measurements indicate a large-signal bias/headroom or dynamic limitation of this implemented detector, rather than a missing rectifier, reference, charge/discharge, or output path.

findings.public_requirement: A transistor-level AGC amplifier and manual or automatic gain selector must produce agc and select mgc or agc onto gc according to mc.
findings.electrical_reason: detp and detn feed the bases of an active NPN differential pair with resistive collector loads and an oa-biased NMOS tail. Its agc_n collector is buffered by Xq_ag_ef and filtered through R_agc_iso/C_agc to form agc, establishing an actual detector-responsive AGC path. The inverter generates mcb, and the two complementary transmission-gate pairs use mc/mcb so that mgc is connected in manual mode while agc is connected in automatic mode without electrically shorting the two sources. The selector tests directly confirm both manual values and the automatic pass-through; the measured active AGC gain of 12.53 V/V confirms gain exists, although it is below the numerical target.

findings.public_requirement: The required TIA, two RF stages, output buffer, detector, AGC, and selector must form a complete receiver whose finalp and finaln outputs meet the nominal, overload, power, and PAM4 requirements.
findings.electrical_reason: There is a continuous differential active signal route from inp/inn through the cascode TIAs and emitter followers, VGA1, VGA2, and the BJT output buffer to outp/outn and hence finalp/finaln. The detector is connected to the receiver signal at bufinp/bufinn through C_ac_p/C_ac_n; its rectified detp/detn outputs feed the AGC amplifier, whose agc output is returned through the selector to gc and both VGA tail-control devices. Supply and bias paths are present throughout. Nominal output bias/offset, overload final offset, and the three positive PAM4 eye openings further corroborate a connected receiver rather than a disconnected decorative collection of local blocks. The reduced PAM4 amplitude is a performance miss, not a signal-path bypass or disconnection.

summary: All six disclosed sections are implemented as electrically connected transistor-level blocks. Several deterministic numerical targets miss, most notably large-signal detector monotonicity and some gain, distortion, and amplitude targets, but the submitted topology provides genuine active paths and controls for each required section rather than a prohibited shortcut, disconnected block, or passive substitution.
